relevance_reason: Narrative review with a dedicated section on MEN5 (MAX). It summarises the phenotype, the mechanism, pituitary involvement and surveillance, but it reports no new primary data.

findings.statement: In a review, Maggacis et al. (2026) stated that inactivating variants of the MAX gene (chromosome 14q23.3), which encodes a 160-amino acid transcription factor, cause MEN5 syndrome. The syndrome was designated in 2021, after MAX variants had been associated with phaeochromocytoma/paraganglioma (PPGL) since 2011. They listed PPGL and pituitary adenoma as cardinal features, and parathyroid adenomas and pancreatic NET as less common features.
quotes: Inactivating variants of the MAX gene (chromosome 14q23.3; encoding MAX, a 160-amino acid transcription factor) produce MEN5 syndrome, designated by Seabrook et al. in 2021, following the association of MAX variants with PPGL since 2011.
MEN5 syndrome | MAX | PPGL, pituitary adenoma | Parathyroid adenomas, pancreatic NET | |

findings.statement: Maggacis et al. (2026) explained that inactivating MAX variants prevent normal activation of the MYC-MAX heterodimer. This leaves MYC function unregulated and drives cell proliferation, differentiation and angiogenesis. They noted that the increased MYC activity is thought to produce a more aggressive subtype of neural crest chromaffin cells.
quotes: Inactivating MAX variants prevent normal activation of the MYC-MAX heterodimer, leading to unregulated MYC function and subsequent cell proliferation, differentiation and angiogenesis; it is thought that the increased MYC activity leads to the development of a more aggressive subtype of neural crest chromaffin cells.

findings.statement: Maggacis et al. (2026) summarised a series of 109 patients from 87 families with MAX variants. Of these patients, 92.7% developed phaeochromocytoma, which was bilateral in 58.4% and metastatic in 18.8%; mean age at diagnosis was 32.8 years. Co-existing tumours included paraganglioma (10.9%), functioning pituitary adenoma (8.3%) and other neuroendocrine tumours (10.9%). The catecholamine phenotype was generally mixed noradrenaline and adrenaline secretion.
quotes: A series of 109 patients from 87 families found that 92.7% developed phaeochromocytoma, of which 58.4% were bilateral and 18.8% were metastatic; mean age at diagnosis was 32.8 ± 12.6 years and other tumours often co-existed, including paraganglioma (10.9%), functioning pituitary adenoma (8.3%) or other neuroendocrine tumour (10.9%).
with the catecholamine phenotype generally being mixed noradrenaline and adrenaline secretion

findings.statement: Maggacis et al. (2026) stated that the exact prevalence of MEN5 is unknown, but that it is thought to account for 0.8 to 1.9% of PPGL.
quotes: The exact prevalence of MEN5 syndrome is unknown, but it is thought to account for 0.8–1.9% of PPGL.

findings.statement: Maggacis et al. (2026) noted that both loss of MAX immunohistochemical staining and loss of heterozygosity have been found in MAX-related phaeochromocytoma. They suggested these tests may help when a causative MAX variant is suspected, for example with a germline MAX variant of uncertain significance.
quotes: Both loss of immunohistochemical staining for MAX and loss of heterozygosity have been identified in MAX-related phaeochromocytoma; thus, such tests may be pursued in clinical settings suspicious for a causative MAX variant, e.g. in the case of a germline MAX variant of uncertain significance.

findings.statement: Maggacis et al. (2026) noted that there are no formal guidelines for MEN5 surveillance. An international consensus statement on childhood PPGL recommended the following for carriers of a pathogenic germline MAX variant: annual clinical assessment from age 10 years, plus annual plasma metanephrines and MRI from neck to pelvis every 2 to 3 years, starting at presentation or from age 15 years.
quotes: Critically, there are no formal guidelines regarding comprehensive MEN5 surveillance; however, an international consensus statement regarding childhood PPGL management recommended that surveillance for those with a known pathogenic germline MAX variant should include annual clinical assessment from the age of 10 years, and annual plasma metanephrines and 2–3 yearly MRI neck to pelvis from presentation or from the age of 15 years.

findings.statement: Maggacis et al. (2026) cited a patient with the pathogenic MAX variant c.97C>T (p.Arg33*) who had bilateral asynchronous phaeochromocytoma and a pituitary adenoma co-secreting prolactin and growth hormone. The adenoma showed loss of MAX expression on immunohistochemistry, consistent with loss of heterozygosity in the tumour.
quotes: in a patient with a pathogenic MAX variant, c.97C>T (p.Arg33*), and bilateral asynchronous phaeochromocytoma, a prolactin/growth hormone co-secreting pituitary adenoma demonstrated loss of MAX expression on immunohistochemistry, consistent with tumoural loss of heterozygosity.

findings.statement: Maggacis et al. (2026) cited a reported case of pituitary gigantism in a patient carrying a novel MAX variant, c.228delG (p.Asn78Thrfs*92).
quotes: Pituitary gigantism has recently been documented to occur, identified in a case with a novel variant MAX c.228delG (p.Asn78Thrfs*92).

findings.statement: Maggacis et al. (2026) noted that pituitary adenomas associated with MAX variants tend to be functioning and are typically of PIT1 lineage, secreting growth hormone and/or prolactin. MAX-associated lactotroph adenomas tend to respond well to dopamine agonists, whereas somatotrophinomas tend to need multiple lines of therapy. The authors added that the broader phenotype of MAX variants has been hypothesised to include other neural crest-lineage diseases, such as ganglioneuroma, neuroblastoma, parathyroid adenoma, chondrosarcoma, myelolipoma and lung adenocarcinoma.
quotes: Pituitary adenomas associated with MAX variants tend to be functioning, typically of PIT1 lineage with evidence of growth hormone and/or prolactin secretion.
MAX-associated lactotroph adenomas tend to respond well to dopamine agonist therapy, whereas MAX-associated somatotrophinoma tends to require multiple lines of therapy.

The broader phenotype of MAX variants has been hypothesised to additionally comprise other neural crest cell-lineage diseases, including ganglioneuromas, neuroblastomas, parathyroid adenomas, chondrosarcoma, myelolipoma and lung adenocarcinoma.

relevance_reason: A systematic review that summarizes the tumor spectrum and clinical features of 127 reported patients with MEN5 caused by germline MAX mutations.

findings.statement: Charoenngam et al. (2026) described multiple endocrine neoplasia type 5 (MEN5) as a newly recognized entity caused by heterozygous inactivating germline mutations in the MAX gene.
quotes: multiple endocrine neoplasia type 5 (MEN5) caused by heterozygous inactivating germline MYC-associated factor X (MAX) mutations
this newly recognized entity

findings.statement: Charoenngam et al. (2026) performed a systematic review of 45 studies covering 127 patients with germline MAX mutations. The median age at first tumor diagnosis was 29 years, and 37.0% of patients were women. The most frequent tumors were pheochromocytoma (112 patients; median age at diagnosis 31 years), pituitary adenoma (11 patients; median age 33 years), and paraganglioma (10 patients; median age 43 years). Among the pheochromocytomas, 38.3% were unilateral and 27.6% were metastatic, and most secreted norepinephrine.
quotes: Of 621 records screened, 45 studies comprising 127 patients with germline MAX mutations met the eligibility criteria. The median age at first tumor diagnosis was 29 years (23.0 - 39.0) and 37.0% were women.
The most frequent tumors were pheochromocytoma (PCC, N = 112), pituitary adenoma (N = 11), and paraganglioma (N = 10), with median ages at diagnosis of 31.0, 33.0, and 43.0 years, respectively.
Among PCCs, 38.3% were unilateral, 27.6% were metastatic, and most were norepinephrine-secreting.

findings.statement: Charoenngam et al. (2026) found evidence implicating MAX loss in the development of paraganglioma, pituitary adenoma, ganglioneuroma, neuroblastoma, pancreatic neuroendocrine tumor, renal oncocytoma, myelolipoma, and liver sarcoma. They considered the causal link between primary hyperparathyroidism and MAX loss to be uncertain.
quotes: Evidence implicating MAX loss in tumorigenesis included paraganglioma, pituitary adenoma, ganglioneuroma, neuroblastoma, pancreatic neuroendocrine tumor, renal oncocytoma, myelolipoma, and liver sarcoma.
The causal association between primary hyperparathyroidism and MAX loss remains uncertain.

relevance_reason: Only the title was available. It is an author correction to a consensus statement on phaeochromocytoma and paraganglioma in children. It reports no patients, variants or data about MEN5 (MAX-related multiple endocrine neoplasia type V) that a curator could cite.
Reports a new MEN5 kindred with a novel germline MAX frameshift variant, expanding the phenotype to pituitary gigantism and myelolipoma.

findings.statement: Haider et al. (2025) described a large kindred with MEN5 caused by a germline MAX variant. The male propositus developed pituitary gigantism from a mixed growth hormone-prolactin-secreting pituitary macroadenoma, which was controlled after 2 surgeries, medical therapy, and radiotherapy. He later developed bilateral and recurrent pheochromocytomas. After his death, an extra-adrenal myelolipoma was found that was negative on MAX immunohistochemistry. The kindred had an extensive history of pheochromocytomas or uncontrolled hypertension. The authors reported this as the first case of pituitary gigantism associated with a MAX pathogenic variant and described myelolipoma as a new disease association in MEN5.
quotes: The propositus had developed pituitary gigantism due to a mixed growth hormone-prolactin secreting pituitary macroadenoma, which was controlled after two surgeries, medical therapy and radiotherapy.
He subsequently developed bilateral and recurrent pheochromocytomas and following his death, an extra-adrenal myelolipoma was identified that was negative on MAX immunohistochemistry.
We report the first case of pituitary gigantism in association with a pathogenic variant in the MAX gene, and characterize myeloplipoma as a new disease-association in MEN5.

findings.statement: In the propositus and in multiple affected and unaffected relatives from an MEN5 kindred, Haider et al. (2025) identified a novel germline heterozygous variant in exon 4 of the MAX gene, c.228delG. The variant was predicted to cause a frameshift and a truncated protein (p.Asn78Thrfs*92). The extra-adrenal myelolipoma was negative on MAX immunohistochemistry.
quotes: We identified a novel germline pathological variant in exon 4 of the MAX gene, c.228delG, which was predicted to lead to a truncated protein (p.Asn78Thrfs*92).
multiple affected and unaffected carriers of the c.228delG MAX pathogenic variant were characterized

findings.statement: Haider et al. (2025) described MEN5 as an emerging syndrome of endocrine and non-endocrine tumors caused by germline pathogenic variants or genomic rearrangements of the MAX gene. MAX variants are mainly associated with risk of pheochromocytoma-paraganglioma, but a growing number of tumors in other organs, including pituitary adenomas, have been linked to them.
quotes: Multiple endocrine neoplasia type 5 (MEN5) is an emerging syndrome of endocrine and non-endocrine tumors caused by germline pathogenic variants or genomic rearrangements of the MAX gene.

relevance_reason: Reports 3 Chinese families with MAX germline variants and pheochromocytoma plus a literature review of 109 carriers, and proposes the designation MEN5.

findings.statement: Lian et al. (2024) concluded that MAX germline mutations may cause a new type of multiple endocrine neoplasia originating from the neural crest, which they suggested be called MEN5.
quotes: In conclusion, MAX germline mutations may cause a new type of MEN originating from the neural crest, which may be called MEN 5.

findings.statement: Lian et al. (2024) described a Chinese man (family A) diagnosed at age 24 years with right pheochromocytoma after more than 2 years of hypertension (200/110 mm Hg), who at age 36 developed a 3.8-cm left adrenal pheochromocytoma with elevated plasma norepinephrine, giving metachronous bilateral pheochromocytoma. No pituitary abnormality or other neuroendocrine tumor was found.
quotes: The proband ( Figures 1 -FA-II-1) was a 24-year-old man who had been diagnosed as having “right PCC” in December 2005 with more than a 2-year history of elevated blood pressure and a right adrenal mass detected 2 weeks previously.
The final diagnosis was a metachronous bilateral PCC.
Biochemical and imaging examinations revealed no evidence of pituitary abnormalities or other related NET.

findings.statement: In the proband of family A with metachronous bilateral pheochromocytoma, Lian et al. (2024) identified a heterozygous nonsense mutation in exon 4 of the MAX gene (c.223C>T, p.R75*; NM_002382.5) by targeted next-generation sequencing of 24 PPGL genes, confirmed by Sanger sequencing. The variant was also carried by his unaffected 13-year-old son. It had a CADD score of 36, and 3D modeling predicted protein truncation.
quotes: Only the proband and his 13-year-old son ( Figures 1 -FA-III-1) carried a heterozygous nonsense mutation in exon 4 of MAX (p.R75*, c.223C>T; NM_002382.5; Figure 2A).
The CADD values of the mutations c.223C>T and c.473A>C were 36 and 25, respectively

findings.statement: Lian et al. (2024) described a 34-year-old Chinese man (family B) with asymptomatic simultaneous bilateral adrenal masses (2.8 and 2.2 cm), normal blood pressure, and normal plasma catecholamines and metanephrines. Bilateral pheochromocytoma was confirmed after adrenal-sparing surgery. Pituitary, neck, and calcium, calcitonin, PTH, GH, and prolactin studies were normal.
quotes: The proband ( Figures 1 -FB-II-1), a 34-year-old male, was admitted to the hospital in December 2021 with bilateral adrenal lesions.
Plasma catecholamine, metanephrine, and normetanephrine levels were within normal limits.
Pathological results confirmed bilateral PCC.

findings.statement: In the proband of family B with bilateral pheochromocytoma, Lian et al. (2024) identified a novel heterozygous frameshift mutation in exon 4 of MAX (c.242_243dupAC, p.Q82Tfs*89). His parents were not tested. 3D modeling predicted shortening of the C terminus.
quotes: the proband (FB-II-1) was found to carry a heterozygous frameshift mutation in exon 4 of MAX (p.Q82Tfs*89, c.242_243dupAC; NM_002382.5; Figure 2B).
The proband refused genetic testing of his parents and his 3-year-old daughter (FB-III-1).

findings.statement: Lian et al. (2024) described a 64-year-old Chinese woman (family C) with occasional paroxysmal headache, elevated plasma norepinephrine, and a 1.9-cm right pheochromocytoma. She carried a novel heterozygous missense mutation in exon 5 of MAX (c.473A>C, p.E158A; CADD 25, REVEL 0.528), predicted to alter the loop domain. The variant was also found in a daughter and a sister, aged 43 and 59 years, who had no biochemical or adrenal CT abnormalities.
quotes: In March 2024, genetic testing revealed a heterozygous missense mutation in exon 5 of MAX in the proband (p.E158A, c.473A>C; NM_002382.5; ( Figure 2C).

The mutation was detected in only one of her daughters and one of her sisters ( Figures 1 -FC-II-3, III-1), but their adrenal CT examination and blood biochemistry, such as plasma catecholamine, metanephrine, and normetanephrine, and so on, showed no abnormalities.

findings.statement: In a literature review of 109 MAX germline mutation carriers from 87 families, Lian et al. (2024) found that 101 (92.7%) developed pheochromocytoma at a mean age of 32.8 years (range, 13-80), with a male-to-female ratio of 1.3:1. Of these, 59 (58.4%) were bilateral (47 simultaneous, 12 metachronous) and 19 (18.8%) were metastatic. Eleven (10.9%) also had thoracic or abdominal paraganglioma, and 1 had isolated head and neck paraganglioma. Catecholamines were elevated in 61 of 63 tested, mostly with a mixed noradrenergic/adrenergic pattern.
quotes: Overall, 101 (92.7%) of the 109 patients developed PCC, with a mean age at diagnosis of 32.8 ± 12.6 years (range, 13–80), and the male-to-female ratio was 1.3:1.
Of these, 59 (58.4%) developed bilateral PCC, with a mean diagnostic age of 31.7 ± 10.2 years (range, 14–55 years), of which 47 had simultaneous PCC and 12 had metachronous bilateral PCC
Nineteen (18.8%) of the patients were diagnosed with metastatic PCC. Eleven (10.9%) had concomitant chest or abdominal PGL, and one presented with head and neck PGL without PCC.

findings.statement: Among the 109 MAX mutation carriers, Lian et al. (2024) found that 9 (8.3%) had pituitary adenomas: growth hormone-secreting tumors in 3, prolactinomas in 4, and mixed adenomas in 1, presenting with acromegaly and/or prolactinoma symptoms. Eleven (10.1%) had other neuroendocrine tumors, including 4 with primary hyperparathyroidism (1 with multifocal parathyroid adenomas), neuroblastoma, ganglioneuroblastoma/ganglioneuroma, C-cell hyperplasia, and pancreatic NET. Seven (6.4%) had non-neuroendocrine tumors such as renal oncocytoma and renal cell carcinoma, and 3 carriers were asymptomatic.
quotes: Overall, nine (8.3%) patients were complicated with pituitary NET (PitNET). Among them, three, four, and one patient had a single increase in growth hormone, prolactin, and both hormone and prolactin concentrations, respectively

Eleven (10.1%) developed other NETs, with an age at diagnosis ranging from 0.7 to 60 years, including seven combined with PCC: four primary hyperparathyroidism(PHPT) cases and each of one case in neuroblastoma, pelvic ganglioneuroblastoma/ganglionoma, and C-cell hyperplasia.

In seven (6.4%) patients, PCC was accompanied by non-NETs, including one each of squamous cell carcinoma of the tongue, papillary thyroid carcinoma, prostate cancer, renal cell carcinoma, renal oncocytoma, breast cancer combined with renal oncocytoma, and chondrosarcoma of the chest combined with multifocal lung adenocarcinoma.

findings.statement: Lian et al. (2024) found 53 distinct MAX germline alterations involving all 5 exons among 87 families, mostly in exons 3 and 4. Nonsense mutations made up 47.7%. The most common mutations were p.R33* (c.97C>T; 21.1%), p.R75* (c.223C>T; 13.8%), and p.A67D (c.200C>A; 7.3%), which the authors suggested may reflect family and/or regional aggregation.
quotes: The three most common mutations were p.R33* (c.97C>T; 21.1%), p.R75* (c.223C>T; 13.8%), and p.A67D (c.200C>A; 7.3%).

Of the 53 MAX germline alterations identified, the most common mutations were nonsense mutations (47.7%), followed by missense mutations (23.8%), large insertions or deletions (14.8%), intronic variants (9.2%), synonymous mutations (1.8%), and gene fusion mutations (2.7%).

findings.statement: Lian et al. (2024) found no significant difference in age at diagnosis, or in rates of pheochromocytoma, metastatic disease, paraganglioma, pituitary adenoma, or other tumors, between carriers of missense and non-missense MAX mutations. They suggested the genotype-phenotype correlation is not strong.
quotes: The results indicated that the high penetrance of MAX mutation-related PCC and relatively high metastatic risk may not be related to MAX mutation types, or that the genotype-phenotype correlation is not strong.

findings.statement: Lian et al. (2024) noted that only 22 (25.3%) of 87 MAX mutation families had a family history of PPGL, and 8 (9.2%) showed a clear paternal family genetic background. They suggested that de novo MAX mutations may be common, estimating a de novo rate of 65.8%.
quotes: Among the 87 families, 22 (25.3%) had a family history of PPGL and eight (9.2%) had a clear paternal family genetic background.
MAX mutations may also have a very high de novo mutation rate (65.8%), and de novo MAX mutations may be a common pathogenic form.

findings.statement: Lian et al. (2024) recommended that all MAX germline mutation carriers receive a comprehensive baseline assessment for neural crest-derived diseases, including PPGL, pituitary adenoma, hyperparathyroidism, and ganglioneuroma/neuroblastoma, with lifelong surveillance that accounts for the risk of bilateral and/or metastatic pheochromocytoma.
quotes: This suggests that all MAX germline mutation carriers should receive a comprehensive baseline assessment of the diversity of neurocrest-derived diseases, such as PPGL, PA, hyperparathyroidism, and ganglioneuroma/neuroblastoma.

relevance_reason: This is a review of the genetics of MEN syndromes. It only mentions that families with MAX mutations show a MEN-like phenotypic spectrum, which suggests a possible MEN5 syndrome. It adds context, not new patient data.

findings.statement: In a review, Sahakian et al. (2024) noted that recently described families carrying a MAX mutation show a phenotypic spectrum that evokes multiple endocrine neoplasia (MEN). MAX is known to predispose to pheochromocytoma and paraganglioma. The authors suggested that these families point to another syndrome, MEN5.
quotes: Lastly, the recent description of families carrying a mutation in MAX, which is known to predispose to the development of pheochromocytoma and paraganglioma, and presents a phenotypic spectrum that evokes MEN, suggests the existence of another syndrome, MEN5.

relevance_reason: Review of the 2022 WHO classification of familial endocrine tumor syndromes. The abstract only says that MEN5 is one of the newly defined familial cancer syndromes. It gives no patients, variants or gene details.

findings.statement: In their overview of the fifth edition of the WHO Classification of Endocrine and Neuroendocrine Tumors, Nosé et al. (2022) described MEN5 as one of the newly defined familial cancer syndromes, along with MAFA-related syndrome and MEN4.
quotes: We describe the newly defined Familial Cancer Syndromes as MAFA-related, MEN4, and MEN5 as well as the newly reported pathological findings in DICER1 syndrome.

relevance_reason: The paper reports two families with germline MAX variants and multiple endocrine tumors, and proposes MAX as a multiple endocrine neoplasia gene (MEN5).

findings.statement: Seabrook et al. (2021) reported an Australian family (family A) in which multiple individuals had pheochromocytoma, including bilateral and metastatic disease, and 2 children, so far without pheochromocytoma, had neuroendocrine tumors: a paravertebral ganglioneuroma in one and an abdominal neuroblastoma in the other. One individual had acromegaly, and immunohistochemistry of that person's pheochromocytoma tissue was positive for growth hormone-releasing hormone. Another individual, whose pheochromocytomas had previously been resected, had pituitary enlargement and elevated IGF-1.
quotes: Family A has multiple individuals with PC (including bilateral and metastatic disease) and 2 children (to date, without PC) with neuroendocrine tumors (paravertebral ganglioneuroma and abdominal neuroblastoma, respectively).
One individual has acromegaly; immunohistochemistry of PC tissue showed positive growth hormone-releasing hormone staining.
Another individual with previously resected PCs has pituitary enlargement and elevated insulin-like growth factor (IGF-1).

phenotypes.hpo_label: Increased circulating insulin-like growth factor 1 concentration

findings.statement: In all members of family A who had pheochromocytoma, and in both children with neuroendocrine tumors, Seabrook et al. (2021) identified a germline heterozygous MAX variant, c.200C>A (p.Ala67Asp). The pheochromocytoma tissue showed loss of heterozygosity. Immunohistochemistry showed loss of MAX staining in the pheochromocytomas and in the other neural crest tumors, and in vitro studies confirmed that the variant causes loss of function.
quotes: A germline MAX variant (c.200C>A, p.Ala67Asp) was identified in all individuals with PC and both children, with loss of heterozygosity in PC tissue.
Immunohistochemistry showed loss of MAX staining in PCs and other neural crest tumors. In vitro studies confirmed the variant as loss of function.

findings.statement: Seabrook et al. (2021) described the proband of a second Australian family (family B), who had bilateral and metastatic pheochromocytoma, a prolactin-producing pituitary tumor, adenomas in multiple parathyroid glands, chondrosarcoma, and multifocal pulmonary adenocarcinomas.
quotes: In Family B, the proband has bilateral and metastatic PC, prolactin-producing pituitary tumor, multigland parathyroid adenomas, chondrosarcoma, and multifocal pulmonary adenocarcinomas.

findings.statement: In the proband of family B, Seabrook et al. (2021) identified a truncating germline MAX variant, c.22G>T (p.Glu8*).
quotes: A truncating germline MAX variant (c.22G>T, p.Glu8*) was identified.

findings.statement: Seabrook et al. (2021) concluded that germline MAX mutations are associated with pheochromocytomas, ganglioneuromas, neuroblastomas, and pituitary neuroendocrine tumors, and possibly with parathyroid adenomas and with the nonendocrine tumors chondrosarcoma and lung adenocarcinoma. They suggested that MAX is a novel multiple endocrine neoplasia gene.
quotes: Germline MAX mutations are associated with PCs, ganglioneuromas, neuroblastomas, pituitary neuroendocrine tumors, and, possibly, parathyroid adenomas, as well as nonendocrine tumors of chondrosarcoma and lung adenocarcinoma, suggesting MAX is a novel multiple endocrine neoplasia gene.

relevance_reason: Reports a three-generation family with pheochromocytoma that carries a germline heterozygous MAX variant (p.Ser49Pro). The variant segregates with disease and the wild-type allele is lost in the tumors. The family also has neuroblastoma, ganglioneuroma and other tumors, and the paper reassigns causality from KIF1B to MAX.

findings.statement: Cardot Bauters et al. (2020) updated a previously reported family with predisposition to pheochromocytoma (PCC) across three generations. The female proband (III-1) developed neuroblastoma of the broad ligament at 17 months. At 22 years she developed a right PCC, a ganglioneuroma at the site of the original neuroblastoma and an ileal schwannoma, followed 6 years later by a left PCC with a mature ganglioneuroma. She later developed a leiomyosarcoma of the mesosigmoid with metastases, a hepatic carcinoma at age 42 and a uterine leiomyoma. Her paternal grandfather had bilateral PCC at age 70.
quotes: the proband III-1 developed NB of the broad ligament at 17 months which was treated by surgery, radiation therapy and chemotherapy. At age 22 years, she developed a right PCC plus a ganglioneuroma at the site of the original NB and also an ileal schwannoma.

Six years later, the patient underwent adrenal surgery for a left PCC associated with a mature ganglioneuroma. At the same time, a well-differentiated leiomyosarcoma arising from the mesosigmoid was detected and surgically removed.
Her paternal grandfather (I-1) had bilateral PCC at 70 years and her father (II-2) had a lung adenocarcinoma at 47 years and prostatic cancer at 54 years.

findings.statement: In the family reported by Cardot Bauters et al. (2020), the proband's youngest brother (III-3) presented at age 31 with a cardiomyopathy complicated by Takotsubo syndrome, which led to the diagnosis of bilateral PCC. His urinary normetanephrines were raised to 8 times the upper limit, while total metanephrines were normal; the authors noted this pattern is reminiscent of MAX-related tumors. The paternal uncle (II-3) developed an 11-mm hypervascular right adrenal nodule at age 56 with strong [18F]-DOPA uptake, which the authors considered suggestive of PCC or an adrenomedullary nodule.
quotes: The proband’s youngest brother (III-3) presented at 31 years with a cardiomyopathy complicated by a Takotsubo’s syndrome which led to the diagnosis of bilateral PCC.

The secretory profile of his tumors consisted of increased urinary normetanephrines at 1979 nmol/mmol of creatinine (8x the upper limit range) with normal total metanephrines at 182 nmol/mmol of creatinine (<190), reminiscent of the pattern observed in patients with a MAX pathogenic variant.

II-3 recently developed, at age 56, a 11-mm hypervascular nodule in his right adrenal which remains clinically silent but strongly uptakes [18F]-DOPA during PET, suggestive of PCC or adrenomedullary nodule.

findings.statement: In a family with PCC, Cardot Bauters et al. (2020) used a next-generation sequencing (NGS) endocrine tumor panel to identify a germline heterozygous MAX variant, c.145T>C (p.Ser49Pro), in the proband's brother (III-3), who had bilateral PCC and was negative for the familial KIF1B variant. The MAX variant was also carried by the proband, her grandfather (both with PCC), her father and her uncle. It was classified as a VUS under ACMG criteria. Both PCCs from III-3 showed loss of the wild-type MAX allele, and structural modeling predicted that the variant is likely deleterious.
quotes: The only heterozygous variant identified was in MAX (NM_002382.5): c.145T>C, p.Ser49Pro.
All also carried the MAX c.145T>C variant at the heterozygous level.
we analyzed the tumor DNAs of patient III-3 and identified loss of the MAX WT allele in both tumors (Fig. 3) suggesting that this variant is indeed responsible for the bilateral PCC in this patient.

findings.statement: Cardot Bauters et al. (2020) found no loss of heterozygosity (LOH) of the wild-type MAX allele in the 2 PCCs of the proband, and Sanger sequencing excluded a second somatic MAX mutation. The authors noted that a high proportion of normal tissue in the samples could not be ruled out as the reason LOH was not detected.
quotes: In contrast, no LOH of the WT allele of MAX was found in the 2 PCCs of the proband (III-1), using DNA obtained from three independent samples, FFPE samples from left and right PCCs (Fig. 3), and one fresh frozen sample from the left PCC
our additional data on this tumor does not allow us to rule out the contribution of high levels of nontumoral tissue to the lack of detectable LOH.

findings.statement: Cardot Bauters et al. (2020) proposed that genetic susceptibility to PCC/PGL in this family is linked to the MAX variant with incomplete penetrance. The father (II-2) carried the variant but developed no adrenal lesion, and his metanephrines remained normal.
quotes: We propose that in this family the genetic susceptibility to PCC/PGL is linked to the MAX nucleotide variant which is however associated with an incomplete penetrance since patient II-2 did not develop any symptomatic adrenal lesion.

findings.statement: Cardot Bauters et al. (2020) concluded that the heritability of PCC in this family, previously attributed to a germline KIF1B variant (c.4442G>A, p.Ser1481Asn), is linked to the MAX variant rather than to KIF1B. They suggested that the KIF1B variant may have contributed to the proband's neuroblastoma, and that her leiomyosarcoma, her hepatic carcinoma and her father's lung adenocarcinoma may be independent of both MAX and KIF1B.
quotes: In this family, the heritability of PCC is linked to the MAX germline variant and not to the KIF1B germline variant which, however, may have contributed to the occurrence of neuroblastoma (NB) in the proband.
Finally, the leiomyosarcoma and hepatic carcinoma of the proband, and her father’s lung adenocarcinoma may be MAX and KIF1B independent.

findings.statement: Whole exome sequencing (WES) of the proband found no pathogenic variants in other PCC/PGL genes or in 30 cancer-predisposition genes. Cardot Bauters et al. (2020) then identified maternally inherited VUS in TFAP2E (p.R363C) and TMEM214 (p.G263S). LOH of the wild-type allele was found for TFAP2E in the proband's uterine leiomyoma and for TMEM214 in her leiomyosarcoma metastases, and the authors suggested these variants may contribute to her non-neural crest tumors.
quotes: Germline variants detected in other genes, TFAP2E and TMEM214, may contribute to the multiple tumors of the proband.

Regarding TFAP2E, LOH of the WT allele was found in the DNA from the uterine leiomyoma whereas no LOH occurred in the parietal and peritoneal metastasis of the leiomyosarcoma (Fig. 4). By contrast, a LOH of the WT allele of TMEM214 was found in the parietal and peritoneal metastasis of the leiomyosarcoma

relevance_reason: The abstract describes the clinical and imaging features of six patients with MAX-related pheochromocytoma (bilateral, multifocal tumours and nodular adrenomedullary hyperplasia). These patients are relevant to the MAX-associated tumour phenotype. Only the abstract was available, and it gives no individual variant details.

findings.statement: Taïeb et al. (2018) studied 6 consecutive patients with MAX-related pheochromocytoma using contrast-enhanced CT and 18F-FDOPA PET/CT. Four were imaged at initial diagnosis and 2 at follow-up. All but 1 patient developed bilateral pheochromocytomas during their lifetime, and the tumours were often multiple within the same gland. The two lesions missed on 18F-FDOPA PET/CT were smaller than 1 cm and corresponded to nodular adrenomedullary hyperplasia.
quotes: All but one patient developed bilateral PHEOs during their lifetime.
In all cases, 18F-FDOPA PET/CT accurately visualized PHEOs that were often multiple within the same gland or bilaterally and detected more adrenal and extra-adrenal lesions than did CT
The two PHEOs missed on 18F-FDOPA PET/CT were <1 cm, corresponding to nodular adrenomedullary hyperplasia.

phenotypes.text: multifocal pheochromocytoma within the same gland

findings.statement: Taïeb et al. (2018) reported 5 different mutations in the MAX gene among their 6 patients with pheochromocytoma. In silico analyses predicted that these mutations disrupt the Max/Myc interaction and/or abolish binding to DNA.
quotes: The patients had five different mutations in the MAX gene that caused disruption of Max/Myc interaction and/or abolished interaction with DNA based on in silico analyses.

findings.statement: Taïeb et al. (2018) found that 18F-FDOPA PET/CT detected more lesions than CT/MRI in MAX-related pheochromocytoma (per-lesion sensitivity 90.9% vs 52.4%). 68Ga-DOTATATE PET/CT detected fewer lesions than 18F-FDOPA in 1 of 3 patients. 18F-FDG PET/CT was only faintly positive in 2 of 4 patients and underestimated extra-adrenal lesions in 1 patient. The authors concluded that 18F-FDOPA PET/CT should be considered the first-line functional imaging modality for these patients.
quotes: per-lesion sensitivity, 90.9% vs 52.4% for CT/magnetic resonance imaging
18F-fluorodeoxyglucose PET/CT was only faintly positive in two of four patients with underestimation of extra-adrenal lesions in one patient.
18F-FDOPA PET/CT should be considered as the first-line functional imaging modality for diagnostic or follow-up evaluations for these patients.

relevance_reason: This is the original report linking germline MAX mutations to hereditary pheochromocytoma, the phenotype covered by MEN5.

findings.statement: Comino-Méndez et al. (2011) sequenced the exomes of 3 unrelated individuals with hereditary pheochromocytoma who did not have mutations in known susceptibility genes, and found mutations in the MAX gene. The tumors lacked MAX protein and showed loss of heterozygosity caused by uniparental disomy, which supported a role for MAX alterations in the disease.
quotes: We sequenced the exomes of three unrelated individuals with hereditary PCC (cases) and identified mutations in MAX, the MYC associated factor X gene.
Absence of MAX protein in the tumors and loss of heterozygosity caused by uniparental disomy supported the involvement of MAX alterations in the disease.

findings.statement: In a follow-up study of a selected series of 59 patients with pheochromocytoma, Comino-Méndez et al. (2011) found 5 additional MAX mutations.
quotes: A follow-up study of a selected series of 59 cases with PCC identified five additional MAX mutations

findings.statement: Comino-Méndez et al. (2011) suggested that MAX mutations were associated with malignant outcome in pheochromocytoma. They also suggested that loss of MAX function correlated with metastatic potential.
quotes: suggested an association with malignant outcome and preferential paternal transmission of MAX mutations
suggests that loss of MAX function is correlated with metastatic potential

findings.statement: Comino-Méndez et al. (2011) suggested that MAX mutations are preferentially transmitted through the father.
quotes: suggested an association with malignant outcome and preferential paternal transmission of MAX mutations

findings.statement: Comino-Méndez et al. (2011) proposed that the MYC-MAX-MXD1 network is involved in the development and progression of neural crest cell tumors. They cited 2 lines of support: rat pheochromocytoma (PC12) cells lack functional MAX, and MYCN is amplified in neuroblastoma.
quotes: The involvement of the MYC-MAX-MXD1 network in the development and progression of neural crest cell tumors is further supported by the lack of functional MAX in rat PCC (PC12) cells and by the amplification of MYCN in neuroblastoma

relevance_reason: The abstract reports inherited loss-of-function KIF1B-beta missense mutations in pheochromocytomas and neuroblastomas, along with functional evidence placing KIF1B-beta downstream of EglN3 in neuronal apoptosis.

findings.statement: Schlisio et al. (2008) identified inherited loss-of-function missense mutations in KIF1B-beta in neuroblastomas and pheochromocytomas, and an acquired loss-of-function mutation in a medulloblastoma. They argued that KIF1B-beta is a pathogenic target of the 1p36 deletions that are frequent in neural crest-derived tumors.
quotes: We identified inherited loss-of-function KIF1Bbeta missense mutations in neuroblastomas and pheochromocytomas and an acquired loss-of-function mutation in a medulloblastoma, arguing that KIF1Bbeta is a pathogenic target of these deletions.

findings.statement: Using an unbiased shRNA screen, Schlisio et al. (2008) found that the kinesin KIF1B-beta acts downstream of the EglN3 prolyl hydroxylase. They showed that KIF1B-beta is both necessary and sufficient for neuronal apoptosis when nerve growth factor (NGF) becomes limiting. This is a developmental apoptotic pathway on which VHL, NF1, RET, SDHB and SDHD act.
quotes: Using an unbiased shRNA screen we found that the kinesin KIF1Bbeta acts downstream from EglN3 and is both necessary and sufficient for neuronal apoptosis when NGF becomes limiting.

VHL, NF-1, c-Ret, and Succinate Dehydrogenase Subunits B and D act on a developmental apoptotic pathway that is activated when nerve growth factor (NGF) becomes limiting for neuronal progenitor cells and requires the EglN3 prolyl hydroxylase as a downstream effector.

findings.statement: Schlisio et al. (2008) noted that KIF1B-beta maps to chromosome 1p36.2, a region frequently deleted in neural crest-derived tumors, including neuroblastomas.
quotes: KIF1Bbeta maps to chromosome 1p36.2, which is frequently deleted in neural crest-derived tumors including neuroblastomas.
